translations.en: A message was written on the wall.
The letters had faded beyond reading.
Two pieces of bread.
One bottle of milk.
The handwriting had a childish quality.
Something was written on the floor...
"Great is the wisdom of those who came before."
"Yet those who would decipher it shall be tested."
That monster scared me so much
that I ran all over the place.
The final line was carved deeply.
"Where the hell am I?!"
A lukewarm breeze suddenly brushed your cheek from behind!
Perhaps you should take a look around.
"Grrrrrrrrrr..."
A monster's low, rumbling growl
echoed through the labyrinth.
It seemed to come from the labyrinth's deepest reaches.
You found a door.
It was slightly ajar,
so you might be able to peek inside.
You noticed words written on the door.
"The Door That Never Opens." Coming soon.
A glittering, lavishly decorated sign stood there.
Hello!
We eagerly await the arrival of our dear adventurers.
"Sincerely, All the Monsters."
A soot-stained note lay at your feet.
You picked it up and read it.
In a creepy place like this,
that idiot is sitting there drinking wine.
My companion really doesn't have a care in the world.
That was what the note said, scrawled in rough handwriting.
You found a stone monument.
It looked as though it had been brought here recently.
"My beloved Jane. With this body, I shal..."
That was all that had been carved into the stone.
Was it some kind of code?
You could hear a mysterious voice...
"Sometimes you must change your approach."
The mysterious voice grew fainter until it faded away.
Something resembling letters was written on the wall.
"Go backward here to reach the exit."
That was about all you could make out if you strained to read it.
You noticed a sign hanging from the ceiling.
It read:
"Those who live longest are not the brave,
but those who are a little afraid."
You found a stone tablet carelessly abandoned.
There were signs of carvings on its surface.
It bore unfamiliar, letterlike symbols
and drawings that resembled monsters.
You could not understand what the tablet meant...
You found an animal's bones at your feet.
They looked dried out and brittle.
A note lay beside the path.
You picked it up and read it.
My companion keeps leaving animal bones along the way,
saying they'll serve as markers...
I nod along, barely hiding my disbelief,
but I take notes so we won't lose our way back.
Words were written on the wall...
"We've already been this way."
Beneath the words were countless marks of all kinds.
You could find no space left to add your own mark.
A sheet of parchment lay in the passage.
You picked it up and read it.
This bread is delicious. Plain black bread!
Who knew it could taste this good?!
When I get out of this labyrinth,
I want to eat until I'm stuffed.
There were other impassioned words on the parchment,
but nothing that seemed important.
Letters were faintly carved into the floor...
Feel the flow of the wind.
That wind leads to the exit.
Words were written on the wall before you.
Perhaps so they would not be overlooked,
they had been written in large, thick letters.
"Dead End."
